Curiosity measured about 0.67 mSv/day at Gale. Dose raises allele-flip chance in crosses. Alleles themselves are game rules.

title: First seed in the ground
text: NASA’s BVAD budgets about 0.8 kg dry food solids per crew member per day for life support planning.
survival: Stored rations only buy time. Local planting is how a stranded crew turns sols into calories before rescue.

title: Soil ready to farm
text: Phoenix measured about 0.4–0.6 wt% perchlorate in polar soil—salts that make untreated regolith unsafe for food crops.
survival: Washing (or going hydroponic) is the difference between a harvest you can eat and biomass you must discard.

title: First harvest
text: BVAD crop tables set growth periods and edible productivity so greenhouse area can be sized against crew food need.
survival: Each successful harvest resets the hunger clock. Without it, health falls and the rescue deadline becomes a starvation race.

title: Lettuce on the menu
text: BVAD lists lettuce at about 28 Earth days with modest light demand—one of the faster salad crops in the baseline.
survival: Fast, low-PPF greens bridge gaps when power is tight or dust season cuts solar output.

title: Radish harvest
text: Radish is a short-cycle crop in BVAD tables and has flown in ISS plant habitats as a quick edible.
survival: Quick turnarounds keep pantry mass flowing when you cannot wait months for staples.

title: Potato calories
text: White potato is among the higher dry edible yields in BVAD Table 4-90, but it needs a long growth period.
survival: Staple calories reduce ration dependence—if you plant early enough to finish before storms or rescue.

title: Wheat under lights
text: BVAD wheat needs very high photosynthetic photon flux compared with salad crops—on the order of 115 mol/m²/day.
survival: Wheat pays in calories only if your power system can feed the lamps through dust and night.

title: Tomato crop
text: Tomato appears in BVAD productivity tables as a fruiting crop with multi-week growth and moderate light need.
survival: Fruit crops diversify micronutrients so meals are not just empty calories from staples.

title: Soy protein
text: Soybean is a protein-oriented crop in BVAD planning, with lower edible mass yield than roots or greens.
survival: Protein variety matters once satiety is covered—poor diet quality still drains crew health over sols.

title: Sweet potato staple
text: Sweet potato shows some of the highest dry edible productivity among BVAD table crops.
survival: High dry yield means more mission days of food per greenhouse square meter.

title: Water from ice
text: NASA orbital mapping highlighted regions where ice may lie less than 30 cm underground—reachable with surface systems.
survival: Crew hydration and soil washing both draw the tank. Local ice turns a finite lander load into a renewable loop.

title: Power buffer
text: InSight lost nearly all of its usable solar power to dust accumulation before the mission ended.
survival: Batteries and cleaning buy sols of life support when panels go dark in a storm.

title: Storm reserves
text: Global dust storms can drive optical depth high enough to starve solar-powered systems for weeks.
survival: Stored watt-hours are the difference between shedding greenhouses and keeping the habitat online.

title: Breeding under dose
text: Curiosity’s RAD instrument measured about 0.67 mSv/day of ionizing dose at Gale Crater.
survival: In this game, dose and solar particle events raise allele-flip chance—an educational model, not real Mars plant genetics.
